verses.text: Abraham was now very old, and the LORD had blessed him in every way.
Abraham said to his oldest servant, the one in charge of everything he owned, "Put your hand under my thigh as a sign of a solemn promise.

I want you to make a promise in the name of the LORD, the God of heaven and the God of the earth. Promise that you will not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, among whom I am living.
Instead, go to my own country and my own relatives, and choose a wife for my son Isaac there."
The servant asked him, "What if the woman is not willing to come back with me to this land? Should I then take your son back to the country you came from?"
"Make sure that you do not take my son back there," Abraham said.

"The LORD, the God of heaven, brought me out of my father's home and my native land. He spoke to me and promised me, 'I will give this land to your descendants.' He will send his angel ahead of you, so that you can find a wife for my son there.
If the woman is not willing to come back with you, then you will be free from this promise. But do not take my son back there."
So the servant put his hand under the thigh of his master Abraham and made a solemn promise to him about this.
Then the servant took ten of his master's camels and set out, taking with him all kinds of good gifts from his master. He travelled to Aram Naharaim, to the town where Nahor lived.
Outside the town he made the camels kneel down near the well. It was evening, the time when the women go out to fetch water.
Then he prayed, "LORD, God of my master Abraham, give me success today, and show kindness to my master Abraham.
Look, I am standing beside this spring, and the young women of the town are coming out to fetch water.

I will say to one of them, 'Please lower your jar so that I can have a drink.' If she says, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too', let her be the one you have chosen for your servant Isaac. That is how I will know that you have shown kindness to my master."
Before he had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She was the daughter of Bethuel, the son of Milcah and Nahor, Abraham's brother.
The young woman was very beautiful, and she had never slept with a man. She went down to the spring, filled her jar and came up again.
The servant hurried to meet her and said, "Please give me a little water from your jar."
"Drink, sir," she said, and she quickly lowered the jar into her hands and gave him a drink.
After she had given him a drink, she said, "I will fetch water for your camels too, until they have had enough to drink."
So she quickly emptied her jar into the trough, ran back to the well to fetch more water, and fetched enough for all his camels.
Without saying a word, the man watched her closely to find out whether or not the LORD had made his journey a success.
When the camels had finished drinking, the man took out a gold nose ring weighing about six grams and two gold bracelets weighing about a hundred and ten grams.
Then he asked, "Whose daughter are you? Please tell me, is there room in your father's house for us to spend the night?"
She answered him, "I am the daughter of Bethuel, the son that Milcah had by Nahor."
And she added, "We have plenty of straw and food for the camels, and room for you to spend the night."
Then the man bowed down and worshipped the LORD.

He said, "Praise be to the LORD, the God of my master Abraham. He has not stopped showing his kindness and faithfulness to my master. As for me, the LORD has led me on the journey to the house of my master's relatives."
The young woman ran and told her mother's household about these things.
Rebekah had a brother named Laban, and he hurried out to the man at the spring.

He had seen the nose ring and the bracelets on his sister's arms, and he had heard Rebekah tell what the man had said to her. So he went out to the man and found him standing by the camels near the spring.
"Come, you who are blessed by the LORD," he said. "Why are you standing out here? I have got the house ready, and a place for the camels."
So the man went to the house, and the camels were unloaded. Straw and food were brought for the camels, and water for him and his men to wash their feet.
Then food was set in front of him, but he said, "I will not eat until I have told you what I have come to say." "Then tell us," Laban said.
So he said, "I am Abraham's servant.
The LORD has blessed my master greatly, and he has become very rich. The LORD has given him sheep and cattle, silver and gold, male and female servants, and camels and donkeys.
My master's wife Sarah gave him a son in her old age, and my master has given him everything he owns.
My master made me promise, saying, 'You must not choose a wife for my son from the daughters of the Canaanites, in whose land I live.
Instead, go to my father's family and to my own relatives, and choose a wife for my son.'
Then I asked my master, 'What if the woman will not come back with me?'
He replied, 'The LORD, whom I have served, will send his angel with you and make your journey a success. You will find a wife for my son from my own relatives and from my father's family.
Then, when you go to my relatives, you will be free from your promise. Even if they refuse to give her to you, you will be free from your promise.'
When I came to the spring today, I said, 'LORD, God of my master Abraham, please make my journey a success.
Look, I am standing beside this spring. If a young woman comes out to fetch water and I say to her, "Please let me drink a little water from your jar",
and if she says to me, "Drink, and I will fetch water for your camels too", let her be the one the LORD has chosen for my master's son.'
Before I had finished praying in my heart, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder. She went down to the spring and fetched water, and I said to her, 'Please give me a drink.'
She quickly lowered her jar from her shoulder and said, 'Drink, and I will give your camels water too.' So I drank, and she gave the camels water too.
I asked her, 'Whose daughter are you?' She said, 'The daughter of Bethuel, the son of Nahor and Milcah.' Then I put the ring in her nose and the bracelets on her arms.
I bowed down and worshipped the LORD. I praised the LORD, the God of my master Abraham, who had led me on the right road to find the granddaughter of my master's brother for his son.
Now, if you will show kindness and faithfulness to my master, tell me. And if not, tell me, so that I will know which way to turn."
Laban and Bethuel answered, "This has come from the LORD. We can say nothing to you, either good or bad.
Here is Rebekah. Take her and go, and let her become the wife of your master's son, as the LORD has said."
When Abraham's servant heard what they said, he bowed down to the ground in front of the LORD.
Then the servant brought out gold and silver jewellery and clothes, and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave expensive gifts to her brother and to her mother.
Then he and the men who were with him ate and drank, and they spent the night there. When they got up the next morning, he said, "Send me back to my master."
But her brother and her mother replied, "Let the young woman stay with us for ten days or so. Then you may go."
But he said to them, "Do not keep me waiting, now that the LORD has made my journey a success. Send me on my way so that I can go back to my master."
Then they said, "Let's call the young woman and ask her what she wants."
So they called Rebekah and asked her, "Will you go with this man?" "I will go," she said.
So they sent their sister Rebekah on her way, together with her nurse, Abraham's servant and his men.
They blessed Rebekah and said to her, "Our sister, may you become the mother of thousands upon thousands. May your descendants take over the cities of their enemies."
Then Rebekah and her servant girls got ready, climbed onto the camels and went with the man. So the servant took Rebekah and left.
Now Isaac had come from Beer Lahai Roi, because he was living in the Negev.
One evening he went out to the field to think and pray. He looked up and saw camels coming.
Rebekah also looked up, and when she saw Isaac, she got down from her camel.
She asked the servant, "Who is that man in the field coming to meet us?" "He is my master," the servant answered. So she took her veil and covered herself.
Then the servant told Isaac everything he had done.
Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah, and he married her. She became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother's death.
